fields.meta_title: Customer Service Automation for Support Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: See what customer service automation handles in four examples, from ticket routing to refund approvals, then build your own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Customer Service Automation Around Your Support Queue
fields.hero_description: Build customer service automation that routes each ticket, answers order questions, and alerts a lead when a reply runs late.
fields.features_heading: The Repeat Work Behind Every Support Queue
fields.features_subheading: Customer service automation is software doing the routine steps of support, while agents keep the calls that need judgment.
fields.feature_1:
Routing rules written in plain sentences

The contact form asks for a topic and an order number, and your routing rules turn those answers into a queue and an owner. Change a rule by describing the new one in a prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Order answers pulled from your store

Status questions are answered from the order record itself. A lookup through your store's API returns the latest shipping status, and the customer sees it before filing a ticket.
fields.feature_3:
A first-reply timer on every ticket

Each priority level carries a first-reply target you choose. When a ticket passes it unanswered, the app moves it up the queue and alerts the lead on shift in Slack or by email.
fields.feature_4:
Refunds over your limit wait for a yes

Agents file refunds and credits from the ticket. Anything at or under your limit is approved right away; anything over it waits until the support manager has looked and said yes.
fields.feature_5:
A live view of every queue

Open tickets, first-reply times, and pending refunds update on one dashboard as they change. Every ticket and every decision is stored in a database you own, ready for your reports.
fields.feature_6:
Your support app's code, yours to keep

Exports the full code of the app, routing rules included, to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Engineers can read every rule as code and change it in the editor they already use.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Automations a Support Team Runs First
fields.tab_content_1:
A double charge goes straight to billing

Delphine Mbeki picks Billing on the Fernwick Home contact form and enters order #48213. The app opens ticket T-20817, pulls her two payments of $64.00 from Stripe onto it, and assigns it to Odette Lam in the billing queue. Delphine gets her ticket number by email before an agent reads a word.
fields.tab_content_2:
No ticket for a question the order record answers

Tomasz Kowal types order #51077 into the help page on his phone. The app reads the order's status from the store's API and shows him where it stands: shipped, and out for delivery today. No ticket is opened, and the lookup is saved to the order in case he writes in later.
fields.tab_content_3:
Four hours without a reply brings in the lead

Keiko Arvidsson's ticket, T-20944, is tagged Priority, and Priority tickets carry a 4-hour first-reply target. Four hours pass with no reply in a busy queue. The app moves T-20944 to the top of the queue and sends Rafael Ndiaye, the team lead on shift, a direct message with an Assign button.
fields.tab_content_4:
Refunds above $150 wait for the support manager

Amara Whitlock's floor lamp arrives cracked, and her agent files a $240 refund from the ticket. Refunds up to $150 clear without review. This one goes to Ilse Barros, the support manager, with the order attached. She approves it in the app, and the log records her name next to the decision.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan customer service automation around your busiest questions, then build and test it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write each rule as a sentence
fields.howto_step_1_des: Export the last 30 days of tickets and tag each one by topic. Sort the topics by volume, then mark the ones whose answer comes straight from a record, such as an order status. Those are the first candidates to automate.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe each automation the way you would brief a new agent: returns older than 30 days go to a lead, and Priority tickets get a reply within 4 hours. Emergent builds the app, its database, and the logic from those sentences.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Connect the help desk, the store, and the payment processor through their APIs. Each automation should read from the record that owns the fact: shipping status from the store, payments from the processor, the customer's plan from the CRM.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Set a first-reply target for each priority level and name who hears about a miss. Pick one person per shift, not a shared channel. A late ticket needs an owner, and a busy channel gives it none.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Decide what waits for a person
fields.howto_step_5_des: Mark the actions that move money or change an account. Refunds over your limit, account closures, and anything a customer disputes should wait for a named approver, with the order and the conversation beside the button.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test on a week of past tickets
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run a week of closed tickets through the automation before it touches a live customer. Check that each one reached the right queue and that every lookup returned the right order. Fix a rule by prompting, then run the week again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live one automation at a time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Start with the order lookup, since it changes no money and no account. Watch two weeks of live tickets, compare first-reply times with the two weeks before, and read every lookup a customer followed up on. Then switch on the next automation.

faq_plan.a: Customer service automation is the use of software to handle routine support tasks with little or no agent involvement. It covers jobs such as sorting new tickets into queues, answering order-status questions from the order record, and chasing replies that run late.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a customer service automation?
faq_plan.a: Describe the support work you want handled in Emergent's AI automation builder, one rule per sentence. Say which topics go to which queue, what a status question should return, and who signs off on a refund above your limit. Emergent builds the app with its database and dashboard, and connects to your help desk and store through their APIs.

faq_plan.q: How is contact center automation different from customer service automation?
faq_plan.a: Contact center automation applies the same idea inside a contact center, which handles phone, email, chat, social media, and text messages. The phone side adds its own work, such as call menus and callback lists. Customer service automation also covers teams that never pick up a phone, like a two-person shop answering email.

faq_plan.q: Is customer experience automation the same as customer service automation?
faq_plan.a: No. Customer experience automation covers the entire customer journey, before and after a purchase, while customer service automation starts when someone asks for help. A welcome email at signup or a reminder before a renewal belongs to the wider set. Each of those is task automation: one action, fired by a date or an event.

faq_plan.q: Is automated customer service the same as a chatbot?
faq_plan.a: No. A chatbot is one front end for it, and automated customer service also covers work the customer never sees: sorting tickets into queues, timing first replies, and holding refunds for approval. You can automate those back-office steps without any chat window.

faq_plan.q: What does call center automation cover?
faq_plan.a: Call center automation covers the phone side of support, the channel a call center is built around. Interactive voice response software greets callers and sends them to the right department. Emergent can build what sits around the call, such as a callback list and notes saved to the ticket, and connect it to the phone platform if that platform has an API.

faq_plan.q: Is helpdesk automation only for IT teams?
faq_plan.a: No. A customer help desk runs on the same moves: rules that route each ticket, timers on first replies, and lookups that answer status questions. An internal IT desk points them at password resets and access requests instead. Outages are a separate job, handled by incident response automation, which pages an on-call engineer instead of adding a ticket to a queue.

faq_plan.q: What should customer support automation leave to a person?
faq_plan.a: Leave a person on conversations where tone matters more than the record: a customer writing in for the third time about one order, a complaint about an agent, or a cancellation. Route those to a named senior agent with the history attached. The automation can still do the lookups behind that agent.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in customer service automation software?
faq_plan.a: Check three things before price: whether it reads from the systems that hold your answers, whether you can change a rule without waiting on a developer, and what happens when ticket volume doubles. Emergent sets no task cap, and a week with twice the tickets keeps running.

faq_plan.q: Can I automate customer service for messages on social media?
faq_plan.a: Yes, on any platform that lets a connected tool read its direct messages. Once a message reaches your queue, give it the same routing and reply targets as email. Scheduling posts and approving drafts is a different job, and it belongs to social media automation.
